messages.text: Traffic spike on the auth service. I'm spreading it across five nodes but response times are still climbing.
Are they hitting the same keys? If every node is doing a cold lookup, we're just multiplying the problem. Send me the request pattern.
Session validation—same token checked repeatedly. I can stick the client to one node, but then that node gets hot.
Sticky is the right idea. Add a shared cache layer in front—token to user, TTL 5 minutes. Invalidation on logout. I'll define the key strategy.
So I route to the cache first, then to app nodes only on miss? Who owns the cache—you or me?
I own the keys and eviction. You own routing. You send traffic; I make sure the hot path is in memory. We're a team.
Fair. What about failover? If the cache node goes down, I need to fail over without drowning the backends.
Run two cache replicas, same key space. You health-check both; if one dies, send traffic to the other. I'll keep them in sync.
Done. I'll update the upstream config. Fast and organized—exactly what I needed.
Anytime. When the next spike hits, we'll be ready. Just keep the distribution even; I hate thundering herds.
Even distribution is my specialty. Talk soon.
